### 1 — Scene
A mixed plate with a cooked bone-in shank, two browned meat-like pieces, several breaded fried pieces, and two sushi rolls. The shank appears to be lamb; the other meat identifications are less certain.

### 2 — Vessel
Likely a **26 cm dinner plate**.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
- Cooked shank meat, likely lamb
- Two coarse-textured browned pieces, likely meatloaf or minced meat
- Breaded fried pieces, possibly chicken or seafood
- Two rice-outside sushi rolls with a crab-like filling
- No separate sauce or dressing is visible; frying oil is included in the fried food’s energy density.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
Heights below are average food thicknesses. Bulk density is the only volume-to-weight adjustment.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shank meat, excluding exposed bone | 8% | 42.5 × 3.5 = 149 ml | 0.95 | 141 g | 250 | 353 kcal |
| Browned minced-meat pieces | 7% | 37.2 × 2.2 = 82 ml | 0.95 | 78 g | 250 | 195 kcal |
| Breaded fried pieces | 10% | 53.1 × 2.0 = 106 ml | 0.85 | 90 g | 280 | 252 kcal |
| Two sushi rolls | 6% | 31.9 × 2.4 = 77 ml | 0.95 | 73 g | 160 | 117 kcal |

The edible items cover approximately **31%** of the plate. Exposed bone occupies another approximately **2%**, giving **33% total coverage**. Bone is excluded from the edible weight and energy estimate.

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **380 g of edible food and 920 kcal** is plausible for the visible portions. Much of the plate remains empty, but the shank is thick and the fried and minced-meat items are energy-dense. Food identification and hidden bone size are the main uncertainties.
